worked_solution:
First, we pull out the factor of $2$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{5x-1}{2x+1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{5x-1}{2(x+\frac{1}{2})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{5x-1}{(x+\frac{1}{2})}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

|  | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $-\frac{1}{2}$ | $5$ | $-1$ |
|  | $↓$ | $-\frac{5}{2}$ |
|  | $5$ | $-\frac{7}{2}$ |

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5x-1}{(x+\frac{1}{2})} & =5-\frac{(\frac{7}{2})}{(x+\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =5-\frac{7}{2(x+\frac{1}{2})} \\  & =5-\frac{7}{2x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{5x-1}{2x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{2}(5-\frac{7}{2x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[5{\int }_{0}^{2}\text{d}x-7{\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{1}{2x+1}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[5x{|}_{0}^{2}-\frac{7}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|2x+1|{|}_{0}^{2}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[5(2-0)-\frac{7}{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|2\cdot 2+1|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|2\cdot 0+1|)] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[10-\frac{7}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡5] \\  & =5-\frac{7}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡5.\end{aligned}
$$
